_comment2: Arc 1600 funicular top. The Funiculaire Arc-en-Ciel (Les Arcs' Express) is the link from Bourg-Saint-Maurice, and it is bidirectional, but in OSM its top station has no edge onto the Les Arcs piste network - everything reachable downhill from it runs back down the valley. Compiled, that made the whole Bourg-Saint-Maurice / Arc 1600 side a 28-node trapped basin: ride up, and nothing gets you onto the mountain. The arrival station is a multi-level building at the resort entrance and skiers walk out of it straight onto the Bois de Saule piste top, so the real-world height difference is stairs inside the station, not a climb. Joined station -> piste top as a flat traverse both ways (79 m, +2 m).
_comment3: Arc 1950 village, Allee du Mont Blanc + its magic carpet. The blue Allee du Mont Blanc ends at 2022 m and the carpet lifts you 39 m back up to 2031 m - but nothing leaves that top, so the pocket is ski-in-and-lap-forever. The village ski-streets (OSM 'Rue de la Piste des Etoiles' and 'Arc 1950') pass 56 m away at 2037 m, and the pipeline built the downhill direction into the pocket (n5361324491 -> n10774972298, skiable_down) while leaving no way back. Reviewed on the map by the user. Both DEMs agree on every node here within 1-2 m, so the 6 m step is real, not a bad sample - this is a short village push at the top of a carpet, which is exactly what the carpet exists for. Added the missing uphill direction only; the downhill one already exists.

addConnectors._why: Magic carpet top (2031 m) -> Arc 1950 village ski-street junction (2037 m), 56 m. One-way up: the reverse already exists as a synthetic skiable_down.

setNodeElevation._why: Montchavin, junction of blue 'Mont Blanc' (w44644749) with red 'Montchavin' (w383420444), 45.54879/6.73595. Our chain reads 1542 and Terrarium 1546; the user read ~1533 off the contours and read the segment's other end (n611005864) as ~1552, which matches our 1550 exactly - so the disagreement is local to this node, not a systematic offset. Both rasters agreeing is not independent evidence (our field averages skadi and Terrarium where they agree within 8 m), so a map reading wins. Load-bearing: at 1542 the Mont Blanc segment drops 8.0 m over 225 m = 3.6%, which passes flatGradeMax (6%) and whose climb is EXACTLY maxTraverseClimb (8 m, passing on <=), so it shipped bidirectional. At 1533 it drops 17 m = 7.6% and both gates fail, leaving it correctly one-way east -> west. Checked for a step: the other three edges at this node (to n611746528 1512, from n610970275 1629, to n566701852 1434) all keep descending and stay well under their colour ceilings, so this is an isolated single-node patch, not the rim of a sunken area.
